title: Example 112: a prod profile sets the hold seat limit under boxoffice.hold.max-seat, a key nothing reads, caught by the configuration block of the boundary contract (B12)
description: The first example of the configuration block of a boundary contract: jvmcontract reads the keys the classes of the Box Office ticketing service and its sibling modules read (placeholders, @ConfigurationProperties, Environment.getProperty), the keys application.yaml sets (profile documents included) and the keys the Spring Boot starters' configuration metadata declares, and writes them cross-checked into src/contract/boundaries.contract. The patch appends a prod profile document with boxoffice.hold.max-seat: 12, one letter from the key the HoldPolicy bean reads; Boot ignores it and production keeps the default of 8. The change is intended, so the runner regenerates the contract and reports as the violation the new ! line: nothing binds it, nearest known key boxoffice.hold.max-seats. The runner compiles the module with Gradle, reads the runtime class path through the build's printRuntimeClasspath task, and runs jvmcontract update then verify with --resources and --classpath; the module's Spring Boot tests need Docker and are recorded as the tests' result.
expected: build.py 112 exits 0: verdict violation, 1 new problem, matches expected
